on 7 March, 2025
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice J. Sreenivas Rao
 Writ Petition No.7018 of 2025
Order:

This writ petition is filed for the following relief:
"... to issue a writ, order or direction, more particularly one in the nature of writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the respondents in harassing the petitioners by issuing impugned notice i.e., For Way Entry/Exit Notice, dated 24.02.2025 issued by the 9th respondent threatening to remove the Rim Jim Dhaba in Sy.Nos.768/EE and 768/HU situated at Rudraram Vidllage Shivar, Patancheru Mandal, Sangareddy District, as illegal, arbitrary, null and void and violation of Article 14 and 21 of the Constitution of India and consequently direct the respondents to withdraw the impugned notice i.e., For Way Entry/Exit Notice, dated 24.02.2025 issued by the 9th respondent by allowing the petitioners to run their business i.e., Rim Jim Dhaba as usual."

2. Heard Sri J. Kanakaiah, learned Senior Counsel representing Sri J.Narendar, learned counsel for the petitioners, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition for respondent Nos.1 and 4 to 6, Sri V.T.Kalyan, learned Standing Counsel for respondent Nos.2 and 3 and learned Government Pleader for Roads and Buildings for respondent Nos.7 to 9.
3.
With the consent of the learned counsel for the parties, the writ petition is being disposed of at the stage of admission 4.

Facts giving rise to filing of this writ petition briefly stated are that the petitioners are the absolute owners and possessors of land to an extent of Ac.1.04 gts, Ac.0.12 gts, Ac.0.28 gts, Ac.0.12 gts,
Ac.0.28 gts and Ac.1.04 gts, in Sy.Nos.768/EE, 787/AA, 791/E, 787/E, 791/EE and 768/HU,
situated at Rudraram Village, Patancheru Mandal, Sangareddy District.

The respondent authorities,
under the guise of widening the National Highway No.65-Hyderabd to Mumbai road, are trying to dispossess the petitioners from the Rim Jim Dhaba in Sy.No.768/HU, situated at Rudraram Village Shvar, Patancheru Mandal, Sangareddy District (herein after referred to as "subject property")
without issuing any notice and without following due procedure as contemplated under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act 30 of 2013).

sentences.text: At that stage, petitioners along with others have approached this Court and filed W.P.No.25292 of 2024 and the same was disposed of on 12.09.2024, directing the respondents therein to follow due procedure in accordance with law.

Thereafter, respondent No.9, without conducting any enquiry and without giving prior notice,
straightaway issued impugned notice dated 24.02.2025, directing the petitioners to remove the Rim Jim Dhaba from the subject property and handover the physical possession.
Pursuant to the said notice, petitioners have submitted detailed explanation on 21.02.2025.

sentences.text: 5. Learned Senior Counsel vehemently contended that pursuant to the impugned notice issued by respondent No.9, petitioners submitted detailed explanation on 21.0.2.2025 and respondent authorities without conducting enquiry and without following due procedure as contemplated under the provisions of the Act 30 of 2013, are trying to dispossess the petitioners from the subject property and the same is in gross violation of principles of natural justice and also violative of 300-A of Constitution of India.

6. Learned Government Pleader for Roads and Buildings submitted that the subject property belongs to Roads and Buildings Department and the petitioners without impleading Roads and Buildings as party respondent earlier filed W.P.No.25292 of 2024.
However, respondent No.9 issued impugned notice dated 24.02.2025, directing the petitioners to remove Rim Jim Dhaba existing in the subject property and hand over the physical possession to him.
However, petitioners without handing over the same, submitted explanation and approached this Court and filed the present writ petition and the same is not maintainable under law.

However, he fairly submitted that if the explanation submitted by the petitioners, dated 21.02.2025 is pending, respondent No.9 will consider the same in accordance with law and requested this Court to grant reasonable time.

7. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition and Sri V.T.Kalyan, learned Standing Counsel, reiterated the very same submissions made by the learned Government Pleader for Roads and Buildings.

8. Having considered the rival submissions made by the respective parties and after perusal of the material available on record, it reveals that the petitioners are claiming right over the subject property and in support of their clam they have filed a copy of pattadar passbooks.

The record further discloses that in earlier round of litigation, this Court disposed of W.P.No.25292 of 2024,
dated 12.09.2024 directing the respondents therein to follow due process of law in accordance with law. The record further reveals that respondent No.9 issued the impugned notice on 24.02.2025,
directing the petitioners to vacate and handover the physical possession of the subject property and pursuant to the said notice, petitioners submitted explanation on 21.02.2025 and the same is pending for consideration.
9. Taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case and the submissions of respective parties, this Court deems it appropriate to dispose of the writ petition, with a direction to respondent No.9 to consider the explanation submitted by the petitioner dated 21.02.2025,
pursuant to the impugned notice dated 24.02.2025 and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, after giving notice and opportunity to the petitioners, including personal hearing, within a period of two (2) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
However, it is made clear that till such time, respondents are directed not to take any coercive steps in respect of Rim Jim dhaba existing in the subject property.
10. With the above direction, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
No costs.
